note: RFC 6811 Section 4 states: 'When a mapping is added or deleted, the implementation MUST re-validate any affected prefixes and run the BGP decision process if needed.' TestHandleROAChangeReValidates asserts a covering mapping addition changes a tracked NotFound route to Valid and enqueues a fresh validation request. Its negative calls the handler again with unchanged cache and tracked state and asserts no queued request; it does not observe unchanged or unaffected routes through the complete daemon or selection stack. TestReValidationAppliesToInstalledRoutes directly exercises stored NotFound routes through typed batch, text batch and accept-routes decisions: each accept rewrites the state to Valid, and the typed rewrite preserves replay sequence seven. Its discard control explicitly sends Accept=false and Ineligible=false and removes that stored route. This is not the current bgp-rpki Invalid-policy rejection, which sends Accept=false and Ineligible=true and retains received bytes. The unit's negative accepts a decision for an unknown prefix, requires an early buffer and leaves the existing route count unchanged without creating the absent route; this is a receive-store boundary, not a full cache-to-selection exchange. Both installed-unit native clean runs passed all five subcases. Forcing applyToInstalled to keep ValidationNotFound caused exactly the typed batch, text batch and accept-routes state assertions to fail with expected Valid and actual NotFound; explicit discard and unknown-prefix controls passed. Replacing only applyDecision's absent-route early-buffer fallback with promoteToInstalled caused only the unknown-prefix subcase to fail: it observed a second stored route, the phantom named prefix and no early buffer, while the other four subcases passed. Both were normal-return semantic failures, not build errors, panic, skip or timeout. The promoted test/plugin/rpki-revalidate-late-sync.ci asserts the real daemon's retained Adj-RIB-In route changes from NotFound/eligible to Invalid/ineligible after its first covering VRP arrives, with nonempty received attribute, next-hop and NLRI fields unchanged. That carrier loads bgp-rpki and bgp-adj-rib-in, not bgp-rib. Its native clean run passed; inverting handleROAChange's decisionRequired guard produced the named observer failure after cache synchronization, with the retained subject still NotFound and eligible. The promoted test/plugin/rpki-revalidate-selected-route.ci and rpki_selected_revalidation.go additionally require real namespace connected reachability and both received prefixes selected before releasing the first covering VRP. After release the explicitly rejected subject remains retained as Invalid/ineligible with identical received bytes and ceases to be selected in BGP best, authoritative Loc-RIB candidates and the selected system view, while the control becomes Valid and remains selected in all three views. The candidate assertion permits the subject to remain as an unselected candidate; it does not claim the candidate is absent. Source review traced handleROAChange, Adj-RIB-In applyToInstalled and validation-change publication, RIBManager.validationChanged, checkRouteBestChange and removeLocRIB. The selected carrier passed a counted own-system per-test-namespace load run with iterations=80, completed=80, executed=80 and no skipped phase. Its fresh native clean run then passed the sole selected test in 5.0 seconds with one executed test and zero skipped phases. Omitting only removeLocRIB in checkRouteBestChange's no-candidates branch produced the named selected-carrier failure in 12.2 seconds: after synchronization the authoritative Loc-RIB still selected subject 10.0.1.0/24 while control 10.0.2.0/24 remained selected. The source reaches that assertion only after both exact retained verdicts, immutable received bytes and the subject-absent/control-present BGP-best check succeed; the broken run does not reach the subsequent selected-system-view check. Both native guest runs stopped normally on Ze's 7.3.0-ze runtime kernel with matching SHA-256, and the red was the observer's semantic selection assertion, not setup, compilation, panic, skip or an outer timeout. All six native records, covering both installed-unit polarities, both tracker polarities and the two promoted functional positives, are retained in rfc/discrimination/rfc6811/RFC6811-4-1.json. These establish bounded mapping-addition, retained-validation and required selection behavior. No mapping-deletion carrier is exercised by any of these checks, so mapping deletion remains unproven and the whole requirement stays weak with no whole-row or whole-RFC credit.
